summary.text: An ice core is a cylinder of ice drilled from an ice sheet or high mountain glacier, built from yearly layers of snow.
Because snow piles up year after year, deeper ice is older, so one core holds ice laid down over a long span of years.
Isotopes in the ice reveal ancient temperatures, and tiny trapped air bubbles show past levels of gases such as carbon dioxide.

items.prompt: A scientist pulls up a long ice core and wants the oldest ice in it. Where should she look?
items.explain: Ice builds up from yearly snow layers, so lower layers are older than upper ones.

items.prompt: How can ice drilled today tell scientists how much carbon dioxide the air held thousands of years ago?

options.label: Old air is sealed in tiny bubbles
The ice's colour changes with the gas
Carbon dioxide freezes into its own layer
Pollen grains store the gas inside them

items.explain: As firn turns to ice, air is sealed into bubbles that capture the atmosphere's makeup at the time.

items.prompt: In Greenland, about how deep does snow turn to bubble-trapping ice, and how old is it by then?
items.explain: At Summit Camp in Greenland the change happens at 77 m, when the ice is about 230 years old.

items.prompt: A team finds a thick band of wind-blown dust deep in a Greenland core. What was the climate likely doing when it formed?
items.explain: Greenland's dust layers match cold, dry periods when wind scoured cold deserts.

items.prompt: Two ice cores come from opposite ends of the planet. How can scientists line up their timelines?

options.label: By assuming both grow one metre a year
By comparing the cores' colours side by side
By matching marks from powerful volcanic eruptions
By counting the bubbles in each core

items.explain: Very powerful eruptions spread material around the globe, leaving a signature in many cores that can sync their time scales.

items.prompt: Researchers want a deep core whose layers are as undisturbed as possible. Where should they drill?
items.explain: Outward flow of the ice can distort layers, so deep cores are best drilled where there is very little flow.
